purpose: Source and reuse-rights triage for current OFD/adamantinoma terminology and natural-history uncertainty; not a clinical evidence synthesis or reference standard.

sources.title: Osteofibrous dysplasia (OFD) and adamantinoma: A comprehensive review and updates
sources.reviewed_content: PubMed metadata and abstract only. The abstract covers OFD clinical, radiological and pathological features and the histopathological spectrum/differential diagnosis of adamantinoma.
sources.reuse_rights: PubMed states open access CC BY International; publisher full-text endpoint returned HTTP 502 in this check, so the article-level license and full text were not revalidated in the payload.
sources.disposition: Follow-up lead only; no cache, registry entry, corpus ingestion, or BTXRD-label mapping. Revisit only after full text and article-level license can be verified.

sources.title: Osteofibrous dysplasia, osteofibrous Dysplasia-Like adamantinoma, and adamantinoma: A Single-center retrospective analysis
sources.reviewed_content: Single-center retrospective study of 50 patients (16 OFD, 27 OFD-AD, 7 AD), with minimum 24-month follow-up. The authors discuss a possible evolutionary relationship; two recurrent lesions were reclassified at later pathology review.
sources.reuse_rights: Article JATS identifies CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; this is outside the corpus builder's explicit CC BY 4.0 allowlist.
limitations: Small, selected single-center series
Reclassification on recurrence does not establish biological transformation
The article's counts vary by available follow-up denominators
sources.disposition: Do not cache or ingest. Retain only as a cited reviewer lead on contested terminology and longitudinal reclassification.

sources.title: Treatment and Management of Osteofibrous Dysplasia Like Adamantinoma - A Single Institution Experience
sources.publication: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America 2026
sources.reviewed_content: Single-institution retrospective chart review spanning 1958-2016. The abstract reports 59 patients, including 43 OFD, 9 OFDLA, 5 ADA, with two mixed/uncertain categories in the full-text cohort table. Authors report no increased progression risk in this limited follow-up.
sources.reuse_rights: Article JATS identifies CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; outside the corpus builder's explicit CC BY 4.0 allowlist.
limitations: Not all OFD diagnoses had confirmatory biopsy
Treatment indications/procedures were not standardized
Very small OFDLA and ADA groups
Historical records span changing diagnostic classifications
Follow-up may miss late events
sources.disposition: Do not cache or ingest. Reviewer context only; does not establish a general natural-history rule.

sources.title: Clinicopathological analysis of osteofibrous dysplasia and adamantinoma: A single institution experience
sources.reviewed_content: Abstract reports 58 tumors reviewed, with 12/58 diagnoses modified after pathology review; radiology impression matched histopathology in 40% of OFD and 60% of adamantinoma. No OFD progression to adamantinoma was observed during median follow-up of 51.15 months (range 4.36-97.94).
sources.reuse_rights: PubMed states Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved; no open license verified.
limitations: Single-center rare-tumor series
Follow-up durations varied, including short follow-up
Not an externally validated imaging classifier
Abstract-level screen for this source triage
sources.disposition: Do not cache or ingest. Specialist follow-up lead; its radiology-pathology concordance is not an estimate of BoneScope performance.

sources.title: Clinical Pathological Features and Cytokeratin Expression Patterns of Osteofibrous Dysplasia in Children
sources.reviewed_content: PubMed abstract reports 49 pathology-confirmed pediatric OFD cases from one hospital (2008-2025), CK positivity in 29/49 (59.1%), and no recurrence/malignant transformation during the reported follow-up.
sources.reuse_rights: No open reuse license verified; publisher full text requires access.
limitations: Single pediatric institution
Follow-up duration is not stated in the abstract
Does not establish adult outcomes or image-only diagnostic performance
Abstract-only review
sources.disposition: Do not cache or ingest; retain as an abstract-level specialist lead only.

sources.title: Genomic Characterization of Classic Adamantinoma, Osteofibrous Dysplasia, and Osteofibrous Dysplasia-like Adamantinoma
sources.reviewed_content: Publisher/PubMed abstract reports a single-center genomic series of 10 tumors: 3 classic adamantinomas, 5 OFDs, and 2 OFD-like adamantinomas. Authors suggest classic adamantinoma and OFD may be genetically distinct; OFD-like delineation findings are exploratory.
sources.reuse_rights: No open reuse license verified; publisher page presents Get rights and content. Full-text reuse rights remain unknown.
limitations: Only 10 cases
Selected pathology-file cohort
Not an externally validated diagnostic classifier
Abstract-level review only
sources.disposition: Do not cache or ingest. Keep as a specialist follow-up lead only.

sources.title: Osteofibrous Dysplasia and Adamantinoma
sources.reviewed_content: English patient-education page states that OFD has not been shown to become cancerous and that there is no good evidence OFD turns into adamantinoma; it describes these entities as distinct. Contributor/update and peer-review clinician names are shown on page.
sources.reuse_rights: Page states AAOS copyright/all rights reserved; no open reuse license verified. Its translation warning says non-English versions may use AI and may not have professional review.
limitations: Patient-education resource, not a primary cohort or evidence-graded clinical guideline
Do not interpret lack of good evidence as proof of no biological relationship
Use English original for source review
sources.disposition: External reviewer context only; do not cache or ingest.

synthesis_limit: Sources differ in case selection, histopathology criteria, historical classification, follow-up, and evidence type. They do not resolve whether/how entities are related and do not map the BTXRD osteofibroma class.
